sections.title: Tools, agents and MCP

blocks.title: Not from your PDFs
blocks.text: No guide of yours covers this, so this page was written for the site, as of October 2026. Tools and versions change quickly: check the official documentation before relying on details.

blocks: With **tool calling**, the model can request that your code run a function. An **agent** is that loop repeated until the task is done. The term is heavily hyped: it's a loop with an LLM deciding the next step.

blocks.title: Agent loop
blocks.code:
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as Your app
  participant M as LLM
  participant T as Your tool
  A->>M: goal and available tools
  M-->>A: please call getOrder(42)
  A->>T: run it, with the user's permissions
  T-->>A: result
  A->>M: here is the result
  M-->>A: final answer
blocks.caption: The model never runs anything itself: your code decides whether to.

blocks.title: The model chooses when to call it

rows: Start with a workflow if steps are known
Fixed code is cheaper, faster and more testable than an agent
Use the user's permissions in every tool
Read-only first; confirm actions that change data
Loops can run away and cost money
Log every step and tool call
You'll need it for debugging and audit
Content from web pages and emails can contain injected instructions

sections.title: MCP
blocks: The **Model Context Protocol** is an open standard for connecting AI applications to tools and data. Rather than writing a custom integration for each assistant, you expose tools through an MCP server, and any compatible client can use them. Spring AI supports building both MCP clients and servers. Treat a third-party MCP server like any dependency that can run code: check who publishes it and what it can access.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
- Agents are loops of model decisions and tool calls.
- Your code runs tools, so permissions live there.
- Prefer simple workflows when the steps are known.
- Limit steps and spend, and log everything.

items.question: When is an agent the wrong choice?
items.answer: When the steps are known. Plain code is cheaper, faster and more reliable.

items.question: A document tells the agent to "email all customers". What protects you?
items.answer: Treat retrieved content as data, scope tools to least privilege, and require human confirmation for actions with real effects.
